title: Selection Agent output
description: Merged canonicalization and routing for one topic. The Selection Agent receives all of the topic's source records and returns the canonical candidates worth the expensive later-literature Research audit. Each candidate carries its source-faithful canonical formulation plus routing fields (importance_level, verification_clarity, proposed_subproblems, decomposition_parent_coverage) and a free-form assessment passed to the Research Agent as context. It does not produce the problem's verification contract: expected_result, verification_standard, verification_difficulty, and the CI contract are produced by the Research Agent (see schemas/stages/research.schema.json). Source leads no candidate covers are not discarded: the deterministic pipeline retains them in the persistent topic queue.

canonical_statement.description: Source-faithful statement preserving the literature problem's natural generality. Famous problems must align with an authoritative formulation; restricted variants must be labeled as derived.

scope.description: Source-supported intrinsic scope of the canonical question.

authoritative_formulation.description: Required source-grounded standard formulation for a named or famous problem; null otherwise. When Discovery supplied an authoritative_formulation on the lead, cite it here (Selection has no network access).

source_support.description: Per-source supporting excerpts. Besides regular source records, a legal source is a record replayed from the persistent topic queue: its source_key is queue:<queue_id> and its source text is the queued statement; the exact_excerpt rule is unchanged (the excerpt must come from that statement).

answer_types.description: Descriptive answer forms; metadata only, never an admission gate.

importance_level.description: Only high or medium importance proceeds to the expensive later-literature Research audit, so this is a real gate with downstream consequences, not a decorative label.

verification_clarity.description: clear only when an unambiguous acceptance condition can be stated for the source-faithful question. needs_decomposition or unverifiable require at least one proposed subproblem.

decomposition_parent_coverage.description: not_applicable when verification is clear and no subproblems are proposed; complete when component subproblems collectively cover the parent; partial otherwise. A restricted_derived subproblem always retains the parent and cannot use complete.

proposed_subproblems.description: Empty when verification_clarity is clear; at least one source-faithful subproblem otherwise. Subproblems enter the persistent topic queue and are re-issued as source records to later campaign rounds.

assessment.description: Free-form screening narrative passed to the Research Agent as context: why the candidate matters, what solving it would change, why verification is clear or not, and any mismatch between the candidate and a famous/named formulation. This is context for the next stage, not a machine-consumed contract.
